statement: Any password at all logs a user in, even a completely wrong one.
Signing in with an email that was never registered still logs you in.
The one registered user can never sign in; entering the exact correct password is always treated as wrong, and any wrong password is accepted.
Clicking "Sign out" sends you back to the login page, but your session cookie still works and you're still actually signed in.
After signing out, you're sent to a page that doesn't exist (/signed-out) instead of back to the sign-in page.
After signing in, the redirect to /orders leads to a 404 instead of the orders page.
Visiting the site's root URL redirects to a broken /order path instead of the real /orders page.
Each order in the list shows the price twice instead of showing the item name and its price.
Every price in the orders list shows as a tiny fraction of the real amount, e.g. $4.8 instead of $480.
Submitting the sign-in form with the password field left out of the request crashes the server with an error page instead of showing "Wrong email or password".
Every sign-in attempt succeeds and lands on the orders page, no matter what email or password you type.
After a failed sign-in, the login page reloads with no error message at all, leaving the user unsure why it didn't work.
Every sign-in reuses the exact same session token, so signing in as anyone signs out (and takes over the session of) whoever was previously signed in on any device.
Submitting the sign-in form does nothing useful; it posts to /signin, a path the server never registered, so the browser gets a 404 instead of signing in.
Clicking "Sign out" fails with a 404 because the form posts to /log-out instead of /logout.
After signing in, the orders page crashes with a server error instead of showing your order list.
The orders page always says "Signed in as User" instead of showing the actual signed-in email address.
After a successful sign-in, you're redirected to the orders page but immediately bounced back to the login screen because no session cookie was ever set.
The whole sign-in service fails to start at all.
Nobody can sign in anymore, even with the exact right password, because the password check now uses different hashing parameters than the stored password hash.
Visiting /login (the address every redirect points to) fails with a Method Not Allowed error; the sign-in page moved to /log-in without updating the redirects.
Submitting the sign-in form always fails with a Method Not Allowed error because the server no longer accepts POST on /login.
Each order in the list is labeled with its price instead of its order number, e.g. "#480" instead of "#2001".
The first order in a customer's history never shows up in their order list.
Visiting /orders without signing in doesn't redirect to the login page anymore; it crashes with a server error because the signed-out guard was removed.
Nobody can sign in anymore, even with the correct password, because the stored salt is now read as raw text instead of the hex bytes it's stored as.
Clicking the "Sign in" button does nothing at all; the form is never submitted.
Clicking "Sign out" does nothing at all; the form never submits so the session stays open.
Signing in always fails with "Wrong email or password", even with correct credentials, because the email field's name no longer matches what the server reads from the form.
The whole sign-in service fails to start because the user database file is corrupted JSON.
Nobody can sign in anymore, even with the correct password, because the login check now hashes the password differently than how it was originally stored.
